text:
Direct evidence for semantic controls: the authors’ [LLM sequential recommendation supplement](https://github.com/dh-r/LLM-Sequential-Recommendation/blob/main/online_material.md) reports that permuting text embeddings across catalog items sharply reduced performance, placing LLM-initialized BERT4Rec below vanilla BERT4Rec. This preserves the embedding collection while breaking item–text alignment, supporting a contribution from aligned semantics. It does not establish word-order sensitivity or exclude every identity shortcut. [WhitenRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.10602) additionally shows that embedding geometry matters: anisotropic text representations can impair item discrimination, so semantic ablations should preserve representation statistics where possible.

For word order, [ACL research on context ablations](https://aclanthology.org/2021.acl-long.70/) distinguishes full word shuffling, within-trigram shuffling, and trigram-order shuffling; these remove different amounts of linguistic information. Applied to item titles, compare original titles against within-title token permutations and an order-invariant token-pooling encoder. These are proposed recommendation controls, rather than findings established by that paper. A fixed shuffled title can still identify an item; across-item title reassignment tests alignment, while within-title shuffling tests order conditional on retained vocabulary.

Recommended experiment: retain the HSTU backbone and compare separately trained, parameter-matched ID-only and title-enhanced variants under identical optimization budgets. Include a random item-code branch matching the text branch’s dimensions and trainability. Permute titles within training-frequency and title-length strata to reduce confounding. Report the fixed macro validation HR@10 plus diagnostic head/tail breakdowns. [TASTE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.14029) reports reduced popularity bias from text matching, motivating frequency-stratified analysis; it does not prove that title gains in this task are semantic. Use controls as separate experiments, without score fusion.
